lessonRef.unitTitle: Decision Analysis and Expected Value Capstone
lessonRef.title: Skill consolidation: empirical probability distributions from data

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A game costs $2 to play. It pays $130 with probability 1/10 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $11; the game is favourable to the player
$13; the game is favourable to the player
$-2; the game is unfavourable to the player
$128; the game is favourable to the player

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $10 and pays out $712 with probability 1/89. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
Option A has expected payoff $17 and Option B has expected payoff $27. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option B; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between three people by rolling a standard die, assigning two faces to each.
choices: Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.

items.prompt: A game costs $9 to play. It pays $224 with probability 1/14 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $215; the game is favourable to the player
$-9; the game is unfavourable to the player
$7; the game is favourable to the player
$16; the game is favourable to the player

choices: Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.

Option A; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between two people using a single fair coin flip.
choices: Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
